FluentBooking_Preview_Help: Available times are based on a sample of this event type's upcoming availability. You can adjust the times offered below.
License_Grace_Period_Help: You are in a grace period, so everything keeps working for now. Updates and support end soon. Renew your license to keep them.
Ticket_Migration_Plugins_Help: If you use another ticketing plugin such as Awesome Support or Support Candy, you can migrate its tickets from this section.
Recaptcha_FluentAuth_Forms_Help: Sign-in and registration forms are handled by the FluentAuth plugin. The settings below only apply to the ticket creation form.
Agent_Mention_Notification_Help: Agents will receive notifications when they are mentioned in replies or internal notes. This cannot be disabled from these settings.
Mcp_Toggle_Help: When enabled, an AI agent such as Claude or ChatGPT can read and work on your support tickets through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The agent acts as the support agent who connects it, and can only do what that agent can do in Fluent Support.
Mcp_Hub_Turn_On_Help: This makes every Fluent plugin that has MCP switched on reachable through one URL. A site administrator reaches all of them; anyone else reaches only the plugins that give them access. It also lets AI apps register themselves and ask a user to sign in. To turn it off again, use FluentHub.
Mcp_Password_Method_Help: Clients sign in with a WordPress application password. Create one from your profile page, then enter your username and the application password below to fill in the snippet. They stay in your browser and are not saved.
Mcp_Who_Can_Connect: Support agents with access to the Fluent Support admin can connect. Customers cannot. Each agent gets only the tools their permissions allow, and a reply an agent sends reaches the customer by email under the connected agent's name.
Email_Piping_Connect_Help: Connect your email address to the Fluent Support email parser so that emails and email replies from your customers are synced with your tickets.
Email_Piping_Confirmation_Help: Your email provider may send a confirmation email for the forwarding setup. It arrives here as a new ticket, so check your latest tickets for the confirmation code.
Help_Scout_Redirect_Url_Help: Add this URL as the Redirection URL of your Help Scout app. Help Scout needs it to authorize the app before the import can start:
Manual_Workflow_Help: A manual workflow does nothing until you run it. When you apply a manual workflow to a ticket, Fluent Support performs all of its actions.
Manual_Workflow_Example: When a customer writes in with a specific question, you run this workflow to send a reply, add a tag and assign the ticket to someone on your team.
Automatic_Workflow_Help: Automatic workflows are always on and run on the ticket events you select. Based on what happens to your tickets and conversations, they run the defined actions automatically.
Automatic_Workflow_Example: When the subject line contains "Bug Report", Fluent Support automatically adds a tag, sends an email to the customer and assigns a support agent.
Ticket_Audit_Empty_Help: Pick a date range and run an audit to get the mood, sentiment score and a one-line summary for every ticket. Tickets that already have a recent audit are skipped automatically.
from_name_help: Applies to replies and outreach emails written by an agent. Automatic emails, such as confirmations, always use the inbox name. The email address stays the same, so customer replies still reach this inbox.
agent_signature_help: The signature is added to emails through the {{agent.signature}} smartcode in your inbox email templates (Inbox Settings > Email Settings). Templates you saved before version 2.4.5 need it added to include the signature.
Remote_Portal_Intro: Host your helpdesk on its own site, for example support.example.com, and let customers create and follow tickets on your main website. Install the Fluent Support Connector on the main site, then connect the two sites here.
Remote_Portal_Legacy_Plugin: The Fluent Support Server plugin is still active. Deactivate it: Remote Portal now replaces it.
Remote_Portal_Switch_Constant: Remote Portal is switched on or off by FLUENT_SUPPORT_REMOTE_PORTAL in wp-config.php.
Remote_Portal_No_App_Passwords: Application Passwords are not available on this site. A security plugin may have turned them off, or the site is not served over HTTPS. The main site cannot connect until they are available.
Remote_Portal_No_Https: This site is not served over HTTPS. Application Passwords and customer data would travel unencrypted.
Remote_Portal_Step_Agent: Create a WordPress user and add it as a support agent with the Sensitive Data, Manage Other Tickets and Manage Settings permissions. To limit what the main site can see, restrict the agent to the mailbox the portal will use. An administrator account also works.
Remote_Portal_Step_Password: Edit that user (Users > Profile) and create an Application Password. Copy it: WordPress shows it only once.
Remote_Portal_Step_Connector: On your main site, install and activate the Fluent Support Connector.
Remote_Portal_Step_Paste: Generate a connection key below. On the main site, open Settings > FluentSupport Client and paste the key with the username and Application Password.
Remote_Portal_Key_Help: The key works once and expires 30 minutes after it was generated. This page updates when the main site connects.
Remote_Portal_Constant_User: Any administrator or agent allowed to act for customers (connection set in wp-config.php)
Remote_Portal_Disconnect_Confirm: Disconnect the main site? Customer widgets stop. Its portal keeps working while it has the Application Password: revoke that from the user's profile to cut it off.
Remote_Portal_Config_Intro: Instead of a connection key, you can set the connection in wp-config.php on both sites. Fill in the portal page and the username, then copy each snippet into the right file. The token below is new and works only once both sites have it.
Remote_Portal_Config_Help: Replace APPLICATION PASSWORD with the Application Password you created for that user on this site. The token must be the same on both sites. Then open the Fluent Support Connector on the main site, choose the portal page, and save.
Remote_Portal_Constant_Incomplete: FLUENT_SUPPORT_PORTAL_BASE_URL is set in wp-config.php, but the connection is incomplete. Also set FLUENT_SUPPORT_REMOTE_API_TOKEN (the same on both sites). If FLUENT_SUPPORT_REMOTE_API_URL is set, it must be on the main site.
Remote_Portal_Constant_Connected: The main site is connected through wp-config.php. Change or remove the constants there to change the connection.
Remote_Portal_Connected_Off: A main site is connected, but Remote Portal is switched off, so the main site cannot reach this site. Switch it on to use the connection.
ticket_tags_promo_description: Create tags like Billing or Bug, add them to tickets, and pull up every ticket on a topic in one click.
ticket_form_promo_description: Choose which fields customers see, make the product required, and suggest knowledge base articles before a ticket is sent.
custom_fields_promo_description: Add your own fields to the ticket form so customers give you order numbers, site addresses or anything else up front, and see the answers on every ticket.
incoming_webhook_promo_description: Point a form, an app or a script at your webhook URL and every submission becomes a ticket in the business box you choose.
telegram_promo_description: Get ticket activity in a Telegram group, channel or inbox, and reply from there without opening the helpdesk.
slack_promo_description: Post ticket activity to a Slack channel so the whole team sees new tickets, customer replies and assignments as they happen.
remote_portal_promo_description: Run your helpdesk on its own site and let customers create and follow tickets on your main website.
ai_integration_promo_description: Connect OpenAI, Google Gemini or Anthropic Claude with your own API key, then draft and refine replies, summarize tickets and read customer sentiment.
auto_close_promo_description: Set how long a ticket may sit without activity, narrow it to certain tags, and let Fluent Support close the rest with a message of your choosing.
workflows_promo_description: Save time by automatically assigning tickets, adding tags, sending replies, and closing tickets based on your rules.
saved_replies_promo_description: Create reusable reply templates for common customer questions and help your team respond faster with consistent answers.
Customer_Search_Quick_Help: Type what you know. The search works out whether it is a name, email or customer ID, and shows the best matches first.
Customer_Search_Field_Syntax_Help: Put a field name and a colon before the value. Combine it with other words to narrow down, for example city:berlin anna. Use quotes for values with spaces: city:"new york". Ticket counts and dates also take > and <, for example tickets:>2 or created:<2026-01-01.
